newsitem.title: GERMANY: DASA sees better result in 1996.
newsitem.headline: DASA sees better result in 1996.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA) said on Thursday that it expected 1996 results to be "substantially better" than the year before, with all but one of its divisions operating in the black.
"DASA's 1996 results will be substantially better than in 1995," chief executive Manfred Bischoff said in remarks he was due to deliver to a news conference.
Publishing preliminary results, DASA said that group turnover rose to 13 billion marks last year from 11.5 billion. Incoming orders surged 54 percent to 16.9 billion marks.

But the figures were not directly comparable with results in the 1995 annual report, which put turnover at 15 billion marks, because of the adoption of the U.S. GAAP accounting standard and the stripping out of results from companies which DASA disposed of in 1996.
Those companies included Dutch plane maker Fokker and German aircraft producer Dornier Luftfahrt.
Gains in turnover resulted mainly from aero-engine and space sector activities, where turnover was up 35 percent and 10.5 percent respectively.
Aircraft turnover, which is based mainly on DASA's Airbus production, increased by 13 percent to six billion marks. Airbus orders trebled last year to 326 aircraft -- worth 23.6 billion marks.
Only the civil and defence systems group suffered a fall in sales of one percent to 2.6 billion marks, and is expected to post a loss.
